description: Inline fitting loss coefficients. Each type maps to one cited fluids 1.3.1 function, evaluated at solve time. 'k' (or 'expansion'/'contraction' for reducers) gives the call: 'function' is a name in fluids.fittings and 'arguments' its keyword arguments. Arguments starting with '$' are filled by the solver: $D = inner diameter of the reference pipe (the segment at pipeIndex), $angle and $radiusRatio = the fitting's fields, $rc = radiusRatio x $D, $D_small / $D_large = the smaller / larger of the two segments a reducer joins. Other values are fixed arguments that define the fitting (e.g. r/D = 1.5 for a long-radius elbow). K is referenced to the velocity in 'referenceDiameter'. A user kOverride always wins and is referenced to pipe pipeIndex (SDD 6.2).

fittings.name: Sudden reducer (contraction or expansion by flow direction)
fittings.source: Expansion: Rennels & Hudson, Pipe Flow (Wiley, 2012), K = (1 - beta^2)^2 on the smaller upstream pipe, via fluids 1.3.1 fluids.fittings.diffuser_sharp. Contraction: Crane Co. TP-410 (2009), K on the smaller downstream pipe, via fluids 1.3.1 fluids.fittings.contraction_sharp(method='Crane')
